name: get_state
description: Returns what the app is doing now, without changing anything: the section on screen (metronome, drone, tuner); the tuner (status idle, starting, listening, permissionDenied or failed, and the last note heard with its cents off); the Harmony section, called drone (playing, note, voicing, chord, progression, style, held tone, current step of a progression); the metronome (playing, tempo, time signature, subdivision, click on 2 and 4) and the settings (reference A, language, note and octave names, the tuner's instrument, in-tune zone and transposition, the circle, screen on, locked gestures). "playing" is true as soon as a start is asked, also while the sound waits for the other one's next bar line. Notes are always written with letters and octave (Bb4), whatever the note names setting. Loudness follows the phone's media volume.

name: open_section
description: Shows a section of the app (also when the gestures are locked). Nothing is started or stopped, except by the tuner: leaving it turns the microphone off, and arriving at it starts listening only if neither the metronome nor Harmony is playing and it was not paused with tuner_stop (the sound is never stopped by arriving; use tuner_start for that).

name: tuner_start
description: Opens the tuner and starts listening through the microphone: it recognises any note played. If the metronome or Harmony is playing, they are paused, as when the dial of the tuner is touched (the player sees a notice with a "Resume" button; nothing resumes by itself). The tuner stops by itself when another section or the settings page opens, or the app goes to the background. The answer says "listening", or why not (permissionDenied, failed); read the note with get_state.

name: tuner_stop
description: Pauses the tuner and turns the microphone off. It stays paused, also when its section or the app comes back, until tuner_start or a touch on its dial. It does not start anything else.

name: drone_play
description: Opens the Harmony section (so the tuner, if listening, stops listening) and plays the piano to practise on: a note, a chord or a progression. Any setting given is applied first. If it is already playing, only the settings change. If the metronome is playing, the piano comes in on the metronome's next bar line, after a countdown shown on screen; "playing" is already true then.

note.description: Note name in English (A, Bb, F#) or Italian (La, Sib, Fa#). The drone always plays it in octave 3 (A3 = 220 Hz with A4 at 440), so an octave number, if given, is ignored.

voicing.description: The note alone, the chord built on it, or a progression in its key (one chord per bar, at the metronome tempo). On screen the note alone is the first entry of the chord menu.

chord.description: The chord played when voicing is "chord": major, minor, dominant (7), major7 (maj7), minor7 (m7), halfDiminished (m7b5), diminished (dim) or sus4.

progression.description: The progression played when voicing is "progression", one chord a bar, each 4, 8 or 12 bars long, from the easiest: pop and rock (I-VI-IV-V, I-IV-V-IV, I-V-VI-IV or the Andalusian cadence, minor), blues (12-bar blues, minor blues) and jazz (II-V-I as Dm7 G7 Cmaj7 Cmaj7, minor II-V-I, I-VI-II-V, circle of fifths in 8 bars as in Autumn Leaves). I-VI-IV-V, the "giro di Do", is the one chosen first.

style.description: How the piano plays the note, chord or progression: struck once a bar (held), on every beat, or as an arpeggio, one note a beat (the piano follows the tempo and time signature of the metronome).

held_tone.description: true for a steady tone instead of the piano struck again and again (the style then does not apply); false for the piano.

flat.description: Writes the note, if it is C# or F#, as Db or Gb (true) or back (false), on the dial and in the chord names. The sound is the same.

song.description: An example song: sets its key, its progression and its tempo (the metronome goes to 4/4 at that tempo), as touching it in the list of example songs does. A note or progression given too is applied after it.

name: drone_stop
description: Stops the Harmony piano (also during the countdown before it comes in). Does not change section.

name: metronome_start
description: Opens the metronome (so the tuner, if listening, stops listening) and starts it, at the tempo given or the current one; the time signature, subdivision and backbeat given are applied first. If it is already playing, only the settings change. If Harmony is playing, the click comes in on the piano's next bar line, after a countdown.

time_signature.description: The bar, with its beats grouped as counted (5/4 as 3+2, 7/8 as 2+2+3). Applied before bpm, which is checked against it.

bpm.description: Beats per minute of the note value the tempo counts in the current time signature: quarter notes in x/4, dotted quarters in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8, eighth notes in 7/8. At most 250, or 400 in 7/8.

subdivision.description: What fills each beat, with softer clicks: quarters (the beat alone), eighths, swing_eighths, triplets, sixteenths or swing_sixteenths. The swung ones are written straight and played long-short, as MuseScore plays "Swing" (the second note at 60% of the pair). With the click on 2 and 4, only beats 2 and 4 are subdivided. Only heard in bars counted in quarter notes.

backbeat.description: Clicks on beats 2 and 4 only, beats 1 and 3 silent, as a jazz hi-hat. Only heard in 2/4 and 4/4.

name: metronome_stop
description: Stops the metronome (also during the countdown before it comes in). Does not change section.

name: metronome_set
description: Changes the time signature, the tempo, what sounds inside each beat or the click on 2 and 4, without starting, stopping or changing section. Give at least one. The settings are remembered for the next launch.

time_signature.description: The bar, with its beats grouped as counted (5/4 as 3+2, 7/8 as 2+2+3). Applied before bpm, which is checked against it.

bpm.description: Beats per minute of the note value the tempo counts in the current time signature: quarter notes in x/4, dotted quarters in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8, eighth notes in 7/8. At most 250, or 400 in 7/8.

The swung ones are written straight and played long-short, as MuseScore plays "Swing" (the second note at 60% of the pair). With the click on 2 and 4, only beats 2 and 4 are subdivided. Only heard in bars counted in quarter notes.

backbeat.description: Clicks on beats 2 and 4 only, beats 1 and 3 silent, as a jazz hi-hat. Only heard in 2/4 and 4/4.

name: drone_set
description: Changes the Harmony settings (give any of them) without starting, stopping or changing section.

name: set_reference_pitch
description: Sets the frequency of A4, shared by the tuner and the drone, and saves it in the settings. Whole hertz only.

hz.description: Frequency of A4 in Hz, a whole number.

name: settings_set
description: Changes and saves the app settings (give any of them): the language, how note names and octaves are written, the tuner (instrument, in-tune zone, the key of a transposing instrument), the Harmony circle, keeping the screen on and locking the swipes between sections. All the values are checked first: if one is wrong, none is applied.

transposition.description: The chromatic tuner names the written note of an instrument in this key (B♭ clarinet or trumpet, E♭ alto sax, F horn); "c" names notes as they sound.

note_names.description: "solfege" is Do Re Mi, "letters" is C D E, "auto" follows the app language. The octave numbers are set apart, with octave_numbering.

octave_numbering.description: How octaves are numbered on screen: scientific (A4 = 440 Hz, the low E of a bass is E1) or italian (La3 = 440 Hz, Mi0).

tuner_instrument.description: What the tuner tunes: any note (chromatic), or the open strings of an instrument, shown with their string number. Bass listens up to 700 Hz, the others up to 2800 Hz.

in_tune_cents.description: How close a note must be, in cents either way, to count as in tune.

circle_layout.description: How the twelve notes are laid round the Harmony dial: by fifths, or in semitones as on the fingerboard.

keep_screen_on.description: Keeps the screen on while something plays or the tuner listens.

lock_gestures.description: Turns off swiping between sections (the tabs and the actions still work).
